The Trump administration has spent millions on campaign-style ad spots over the last week.

Actual Article Body:
The Washington Sun

White House

The Trump administration has spent millions on campaign-style ad spots over the last week.

President Donald Trump defended the ads Wednesday, saying he’s promoting the country. (Alex Brandon/AP)

By Gavin J. Quinton

September 30, 2026
                                                10:35 p.m.

U.S. taxpayers funded another high-octane, government-sponsored ad across cable news channels premiering Wednesday night, this time promoting President Donald Trump’s war with Iran.

The spot, first flagged by political ad-buying firm Medium Buying, flaunts a flashing series of missile strikes and F-22 jet acrobatics interlaced over bombastic speech from Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

“This regime will soon learn that no one should challenge the strength and might of the United States armed forces,” Trump narrates.

Column: Chicago White Sox have made converts out of everyone — including Jerry Reinsdorf

The Chicago White Sox’s first postseason series win since the 2005 World Series vindicated Chairman Jerry Reinsdorf for promoting Chris Getz to general manager.

HOUSTON — The Chicago White Sox made believers out of skeptics this season, going from three straight seasons of 100-plus losses to the 2026 postseason.

And now they’re in the American League Division Series after sweeping the Houston Astros in a best-of-three wild-card series.

Whether Pope Leo XIV had anything to do with it is anyone’s guess, but Chairman Jerry Reinsdorf didn’t need any more convincing.

“I’m going to convert,” Reinsdorf said in the champagne-soaked visitors clubhouse at Daikin Park.

Twenty-one years ago Reinsdorf was celebrating a World Series championship at this ballpark, which he admitted “was a pretty good night too.” This one also was “pretty good,” albeit on a smaller scale.
